title: Nested Types: A Deck of Cards
hints: Types can be nested inside other types.
Nest `Suit` and `Rank` inside `Card`. Build the deck by `flatMap`-ing suits over ranks.
`Suit.allCases.flatMap { suit in Rank.allCases.map { Card(rank: $0, suit: suit) } }`.
jsBridge: Nested types (`Card.Suit`) namespace related types, like TS namespaces or static inner classes. Synthesised `Comparable` for raw-value enums (declaration order) plus `CaseIterable` build a full deck in one line.

compass.q: TS would use separate `Suit` and `Rank` exports. What does nesting (`Card.Suit`) add?
Java static nested classes and enums are similar. Any differences?
For a `Rank: Int` enum, is `<` based on raw values or declaration order?
Nesting is common for `Model.ID`, `View.Style`, `Error`. When does nesting hurt discoverability?
